claims.text: TC4 has an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
TC4 has poor friction and wear performance under extreme conditions.
The proposed intervention consists of controlled heat treatment followed by deposition of a refractory high-entropy-alloy layer.
The initial heat treatment will create a compositional gradient at the TC4 surface.
The initial heat treatment will promote interdiffusion between TC4 and the subsequently deposited coating.
The engineered graded interfacial layer will enhance bonding between TC4 and the refractory HEA coating.
The graded interfacial layer will reduce the mechanical-property mismatch between the TC4 substrate and the HEA coating.
A smooth transition in composition and mechanical properties will reduce residual stresses.
A smooth transition in composition and mechanical properties will reduce stress concentrations.
The refractory HEA layer will increase hardness through its high-entropy microstructure and refractory-element composition.
The refractory HEA layer will increase wear resistance through its high-entropy microstructure and refractory-element composition.
The treatment will increase surface hardness by approximately 20–30% relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will lower wear rate relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will preserve the intrinsic bulk benefits of the TC4 substrate.
The predicted improvements apply under high-contact-stress and friction-wear conditions typical of extreme service.
Performance under milder conditions or different wear modes is unverified.

contradictions.description: The process states that heat treatment creates the graded interfacial layer and promotes interdiffusion before the HEA coating is deposited. Interdiffusion between TC4 and the coating cannot occur during that initial step if the coating is not yet present.
